title: Input-Output Analysis of Quantum Dot SUPER Excitation
authors: Johannes Kerber, Christoph Hotter, Helmut Ritsch, Klaus Mølmer
abstract: The Swing-UP of the quantum EmitteR population (SUPER) two-color pulsed excitation scheme allows for robust and close to 100\% excitation of a two-level quantum emitter using only red detuned light. We analyze the underlying counterintuitive dynamics using a full quantum input-output description of the in- and outgoing light pulses for the case of two coherent free-space input pulses at realistic photon numbers. At the microscopic level, the SUPER mechanism exhibits its nonlinear three-photon Raman-type character, leading to a net photon-number change of $-2$ in one mode and $+1$ in the other, as was first guessed from cavity-enhanced model descriptions at low photon numbers. We confirm that in free space, a sufficiently high pulse photon number, much larger than one, is required to achieve high-fidelity inversion. To treat the large coherent-state amplitudes (photon numbers) relevant for SUPER, we extend the quantum input-output formalism to include a cumulant expansion approach. With an interaction-picture formulation, the few exchanged photons that govern the nontrivial dynamics enable direct full-quantum calculations in truncated Hilbert spaces, including treatments in a displacement frame and for initial Fock-state pulses.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the quantum dynamics of the SUPER excitation scheme in a quantum dot driven by two pulsed lasers. By employing a full quantum input-output formalism and cumulant expansion, the authors confirm the mechanism's inherent multi-photon nature in free space. The results are crucial for understanding high-fidelity quantum control in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the counterintuitive dynamics of the Swing-UP of the quantum Emitter population (SUPER) two-color pulsed excitation scheme.
main_result: The free-space realization confirms the underlying nonlinear three-photon Raman-type character of the SUPER mechanism, requiring high photon numbers for high-fidelity inversion, contrasting with cavity-enhanced models.
method: The analysis employs a full quantum input-output description, extending the formalism with a cumulant expansion approach to handle large coherent-state amplitudes.
model_or_system: The system involves a two-level quantum emitter (TLS) driven by two time-overlapping, far off-resonant red detuned Gaussian pulses, modeled using the SLH formalism and cascade product rules.
key_observables: TLS population inversion ($P$), photon loss/gain ($\langle\Delta\hat{n}angle$), and mean photon numbers ($\langle\hat{n}_iangle$).
important_parameters: Red detuning (several meV below resonance), pulse photon numbers (requiring values much larger than one for free space).
main_assumptions: The formalism assumes the ability to model the pulse dynamics via virtual input/output cavities and utilizes cumulant expansion for large coherent amplitudes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the cascade setup, the population dynamics ($P$) for both two-pulse and single-pulse descriptions, and the resulting photon loss/gain signatures, confirming the $(-2, +1)$ exchange.
paper_structure: The paper builds from a classical reference model to a full quantum input-output description, detailing the cascade Hamiltonian, applying the cumulant expansion in the interaction picture, and comparing results across different pulse representations (two-pulse vs. single-pulse).
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum electrodynamics treatment of coherent light-matter interaction in the weak coupling regime, extending standard cavity QED models to free-space pulsed excitation using advanced input-output formalisms.

The final occupation number ⟨ˆnvi⟩is changed slightly from the initial one ⟨ˆnui⟩. Mode 1 experiences a loss of two photons (-2), whereas mode 2 gains one (+1), which is observed in plot (c).

FIG. 4. In plot (a) the initial mean photon numbers ⟨ˆnui(0)⟩(1/γ) with 1/γ in logarithmic scaling are shown. Reducing the decay rate γ implies a linear increase of ⟨ˆnui(0)⟩∝1/γ. The final TLS population P = ⟨ˆσ+ ˆσ−(Tend)⟩(1/γ) is depicted in plot (b). Here, Tend denotes the time immediately after the SUPER excitation process is over.

FIG. 5. The pure Fock state population dynamics P is compared to the cascaded system in plot (a). The fundamental excitation process without additional oscillatory behavior can be observed clearly. Sim- ilar is the case for the loss/gain functions ⟨∆ˆni⟩in plot (b), which fit almost perfectly. Due to the choice of time steps and size of the trun- cated Fock spaces, small deviations appear. In plot (c) and (d), we visualize that the success of the SUPER scheme in the Fock space full-master equation description is subject to the same 1/γ depen- dence as shown previously. Since the fundamental process is the same, this behavior is expected.
